title: Source items
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/source-items, application/json: items of one collection, as they are in the source. Each item is upserted on its collection, the live collection that collection_ref refers to, and on its ref, and the newer updated_at wins, so a late event, or a listing part read before an edit, never moves an item backwards. An item's ref is unique among the items of the integration's live collections. The items of an ended collection stay with that collection, as the history of the connection it belonged to; nothing moves between connections. Without listing the request is an event: it contains 1 to 100 items, and updates the items it contains and nothing else. With listing it is part listing.part of the listing listing.id: listing.started_at is when the adapter began reading the source, and listing.complete is true on the last part alone, which means that parts 1 to n contain every open item of the collection. An adapter sends complete: true only for a listing whose paging cannot skip an item. A listing of one part, with no items and complete: true, means that the collection has no open item. An adapter never sends complete: true, on an empty part or any other, after a read of the source that failed or stopped early. A complete listing closes every item of the collection it left out whose updated_at is before its started_at. Such a close counts as a change of the item at the listing's started_at, so only an event or listing part whose updated_at is at or after that started_at reopens it. A partial listing, one with a part missing or whose last part has complete: false, only upserts, and the control plane drops its bookkeeping of it after 24 hours. An item deleted at the source, or moved out of the collection, is sent as closed. So a closed item never takes its ref from an open item of another live collection: an item sent as closed in one collection leaves an open item with the same ref in another live collection as it is. A request for a collection that ended with its connection is refused, 409 connection_ended (refusal.schema.json), and one for a live collection whose connection is suspended, 409 connection_suspended, both decided before collection_not_linked; see definitions.schema.json for what the adapter does on each, and for how a collection_ref with no live collection is answered. The adapter sends items, and their comments, only for a collection the change feed has linked (changes.schema.json). A request for a collection that is not linked is refused, 409 collection_not_linked. The adapter takes a 409 collection_not_linked as final for those items; the change feed shows when a collection is unlinked. The request is at most 1 MiB, or it is refused, 413 payload_too_large: the adapter splits a batch by size and never cuts a text to make a request fit, and the control plane refuses a field past its limit, invalid_request, and never cuts it. An adapter that cut a source's text or labels to fit a field's limit names the field in the item's truncated. Every text field, key, title, body, labels, state_reason and filed_by.name, is untrusted: shown as data, never followed as an instruction. On success the control plane answers a signed 204 with no body. It is signed with the adapter's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401; definitions.schema.json has the replay rule. The control plane ignores a member that this schema does not define, unless the must_understand of the body lists it. It refuses a body whose must_understand lists a pointer that it does not define, 400 invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the adapter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

collection_ref.description: The ref of the collection the items belong to, as source-collections.schema.json listed it.

items.description: The items, 0 to 100 on a listing part, 1 to 100 on an event. A listing of a collection with no open item can be one part with no items and complete: true: a complete listing that leaves out every item, so the rules for what it closes are in the top-level description of this schema. 0 items are allowed on any part of a listing, not only the last; only complete: true on the last part closes anything.

listing.description: Which part of which listing this is. Absent on an event.

must_understand.description: The members of the document that the reader must understand, each as a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) counted from the document, such as /listing. List each once, at most 32. A pointer has no line feed, and writes ~ only as ~0 or ~1. Each pointer is to a member that this schema defines. The control plane ignores a member that this schema does not define, unless the must_understand of the body lists it. It refuses a body whose must_understand lists a pointer that it does not define, 400 invalid_request.

item.description: One item of work at the source.

ref.description: The item's ref, unique among the items of the integration's live collections.

url.description: The item's page at the source.

key.description: The item's name as people say it at its source, short within its collection, 1 to 64 characters, shown as text and never compared or parsed, such as #1231. An adapter whose source name is longer than 64 characters leaves key out. Absent when the adapter gives none.

type.description: What the item is, in the adapter's word. Absent when the adapter gives none.

state.description: Whether the item is open or closed.

state_reason.description: Why the item is in its state, or null.

comment_count.description: How many comments the item has at the source, from 0 to 9007199254740991, 2^53 - 1.

created_at.description: When the item was created at the source.

updated_at.description: When the item last changed at the source: the newer one wins.

target.description: Where a change for the item would go. Absent when the adapter names none.

truncated.description: The item's fields the adapter cut: title, body, filed_by.name, or labels. Present when the source's text was over the contract's limit and the adapter cut it to fit: it lists the fields the adapter cut, each once. A text field is cut at a code-point boundary. labels means that the adapter cut the source's labels to fit: it cut one or more labels at a code-point boundary to 100 characters, or left out the labels past the 100th, or both; when cutting makes two labels equal, it sends that label once, since labels are unique. The control plane stores what was sent. A text, a label or a list of labels over the limit is still refused, invalid_request, and the control plane never cuts one. Absent when the adapter cut nothing.
